stories.notes: Empty acceptance criteria with no prior spec. Live preview across GO, UP, and MX contexts is a complex, multi-context real-time feature requiring requirements elaboration (openspec first) followed by testability/security/edge-case hardening (speckit). No existing assignedAgents or hand-curation markers found.

agentContributions.notes: Novel feature — Contentstack Live Preview integration. The central attachment point is useContent (236 callers), the single hook that provides content to the entire app via getContentByKey. Live Preview SDK integration must plug into this hook to push real-time content updates to all consuming components without full page reload. No existing preview infrastructure was found in the explored code.

Openspec provided zero acceptance criteria, so all 12 AC are authored from scratch based on the story title, description, and technical notes. Key design decisions: (1) AC-1/AC-2 cover the core happy-path — SDK connection and real-time content push through useContent. (2) AC-3/AC-9 ensure zero regression for the 236 existing callers when preview is off. (3) AC-4/AC-5/AC-6/AC-11 cover error and edge-case handling — unknown keys, connection drops, malformed payloads, invalid config. (4) AC-7 addresses security — preview must not leak into production bundles. (5) AC-8 ensures multi-site parity (GO, UP, MX). (6) AC-10 covers rapid-update debouncing/race conditions. (7) AC-12 covers performance — async loading must not block render. CAVEAT: I could not read the four referenced files (useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, contentCard.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx) to verify exact data shapes, hook signatures, or existing error-handling patterns. The AC are written to be robust regardless, but refinement after file review is recommended.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: All four manifest paths verified as exact matches across gotransit, upexpress, and metrolinx repos — no missing files. Both agents added non-overlapping value: openspec provided architectural grounding (useContent as the 236-caller integration point, no existing preview infrastructure), while speckit authored 12 acceptance criteria covering happy path, regression safety for existing callers, error/edge-case handling, security (no production leak), multi-site parity, race conditions, and performance. The single verificationCriterion (real-time render without full page reload) is observable and testable, though thin relative to the feature's complexity and the 12 ACs speckit describes in its notes. Per brownfield policy, empty acceptanceCriteria with acceptanceChanged=false is expected and not scored against. The file set is plausible for a Live Preview integration touching the content hook, service layer, content interface, and a Contentstack component. Speckit's caveat about not reading the source files is noted but does not lower the score — the notes provide sufficient guidance for a competent writer to implement and refine during development.
